title: [GR-33796] Non-jlinked-build fixes for breakage after cc11ae1

timeline.body:
Add jdk.scripting.nashorn modules for module look-up on JDK 11.
Target_jdk_nashorn_api_scripting_ClassFilter substitution needs nashorn
target class loaded.

cc11ae1d1fad550424b1fdc0a6cf7e9d6815874a re-ordered arguments passed to
the native image generator. Add -XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions before
actually using any one of those experimental options as that's needed
for some JVMs.

Add relevant modules to the upgraded module path list since for
non-jlinked-builds they are either not there or too old.

Closes #3778

timeline.diff_hunk:
@@ -1932,8 +1932,10 @@ def _get_option_vars():
             return ' '.join(image_config.option_vars)
 
         def _get_launcher_args():
-            if not _jlink_libraries() and _src_jdk_version >= 9:
-                return '-J--add-exports=jdk.internal.vm.ci/jdk.vm.ci.code=jdk.internal.vm.compiler'
+            # Nashorn got removed in JDK 15, added exports for the JVMCI compiler got added
+            # with JDK-8223332 (JDK 13) and JDK-8273547 (11.0.14). Use the larger upper bound.
+            if not _jlink_libraries() and _src_jdk_version >= 9 and _src_jdk_version <= 14:
+                return '-J--add-modules=jdk.scripting.nashorn -J--add-exports=jdk.internal.vm.ci/jdk.vm.ci.code=jdk.internal.vm.compiler'

reply.body: OK, that seems a more elegant way of fixing it. Will fix.

timeline.body:
I really wanted to get rid of stunts like this in the driver (as you can see in the removing of `getBuilderModuleNames` in https://github.com/oracle/graal/pull/3763).

Do we still need this if we solve the `jdk.scripting.nashorn` problems as suggested above?
Or do you have other means of knowing that this is not our GraalVM (i.e. different value for e.g. `com.oracle.svm.driver.NativeImage#graalvmVersion` or `com.oracle.svm.driver.NativeImage#graalvmConfig`)

reply.body:
> I really wanted to get rid of stunts like this in the driver (as you can see in the removing of `getBuilderModuleNames` in #3763).
> 
> Do we still need this if we solve the `jdk.scripting.nashorn` problems as suggested above?

AFAIK, yes. The code which adds extra `--upgrade-module` instructions solves a different problem. Namely truffle/sdk modules not present. For non-jlinked JDKs they come from jars, not the modules in the JDK. I agree this is an ugly hack, but I also didn't want to break your builds.

> Or do you have other means of knowing that this is not our GraalVM (i.e. different value for e.g. `com.oracle.svm.driver.NativeImage#graalvmVersion` or `com.oracle.svm.driver.NativeImage#graalvmConfig`)

I'll look into this. It might work. Good suggestion. Thanks!
As we discussed on slack, this is no longer needed and we are using extra modules on the module path to get around the missing module error when building ni modules, like the native-image-agent.
This would be a partial revert of https://github.com/oracle/graal/commit/cc11ae1d1fad550424b1fdc0a6cf7e9d6815874a. Not sure why the order was changed. @olpaw thoughts on that?
Happy to go either way, but I thought the order change was intentional.

There was some reordering required to allow us to switch to running the imagbuilder on module-path when module-related options are passed to the driver. But this particular change should not cause problems as the value of `useJVMCINativeLibrary` is not dependent on module-related options. Thus @zakkak s suggestion should be followed here.

timeline.message:
Non-jlinked-build fixes for breakage after cc11ae1

Only perform nashorn substitutions if that module is actulally loaded as
it would otherwise affect JDK 9+ builds.

cc11ae1d1fad550424b1fdc0a6cf7e9d6815874a re-ordered arguments passed to
the native image generator. Move code to after compiler specific flags
get added, which includes -XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions.

Add relevant modules to the module path for module-based builds like
'native-image --macro:native-image-agent-library' as not all JDKs have
truffle and sdk modules in the default module path.

Closes #3778

timeline.body: I believe I've fixed the checkstyle warning now. Lets see what the gates tell us. It's now also rebased on latest master, which should fix the gate's failures on debuginfo tests.

I fail to see why we need this check since we know that nashorn is available in JDK <= 14 and we already check for that.
What am I missing?

reply.body:
As @jerboaa observed, there are JDK <= 14 where module `jdk.scripting.nashorn` is not per-default available as a module (i.e. running `java --list-modules` would not show it).

On our side it's not a problem. Our jlinked Java 11 has module `jdk.scripting.nashorn`.

> As @jerboaa observed, there are JDK <= 14 where module `jdk.scripting.nashorn` is not per-default available as a module (i.e. running `java --list-modules` would not show it).

Judging by [@jerboaa's initial patch](https://github.com/oracle/graal/commit/5e4b8fa0c90444115930b09c39b1b999cdd5843f#diff-42623de4b000eeb25f4b626861ebe69fd6fbcb7e9480897d1d5c3ff79cb7eedd) it looks like the assumption was that module `jdk.scripting.nashorn` is indeed available in JDK <= 14

To my understanding the `--list-modules` part was only [meant to check for `org.graalvm` modules](https://github.com/oracle/graal/commit/5e4b8fa0c90444115930b09c39b1b999cdd5843f#diff-9e053bec9eca0799896bd471363fa6aa1df70269e454b89dff1ea5fb844a480cR540) and not for `jdk.scripting.nashorn`.

I suggest we wait for @jerboaa's input on this before pushing it to the merge queue.

> assumption was that module jdk.scripting.nashorn is indeed available in JDK <= 14

There is a difference between available and enabled as I tried to explain above. Forcing module `jdk.scripting.nashorn` onto the list of enabled modules is more intrusive than being able to deal with the absence of `jdk.scripting.nashorn`. See also https://github.com/oracle/graal/pull/3793#discussion_r708293346

> I suggest we wait for @jerboaa's input on this before pushing it to the merge queue.

No problem.
For that reason it's not sufficient to only go by the JDK versions on the substitutions.
OK, I see. I was also able to reproduce the issue with OpenJDK 11.0.12 and 11.0.13. Note, however, that the module appears in `java --list-modules`.

@zakkak pure modular application (like e.g. `native-image-agent-library` nowadays) would need to specify `requires jdk.scripting.nashorn` in their `module-info.java` to have access to it. Otherwise `jdk.scripting.nashorn` is just not available for them.

Thus if you build an image on the module path (i.e. use `-p` `-m` options instead of `-cp` or `-jar` with native-image) it is not a given that `jdk.scripting.nashorn` will be available.
